Bill Simplification

Redesigning the Airtel app bill so customers can understand the bill by themselves easily.

Role
Lead Product Designer
Brief from
Customer experience team
Phase 1 scope
Airtel app bill (digital)
Team
PM, CX, billing tech, care ops
The brief

A request from the customer experience team

"Customers find the current bill very complicated to understand. Charges aren't grouped, people can't see why they're paying more than the plan they bought, and the app and the PDF bill should use the same groups and words."

Brief from the customer experience team
Scope

Start with the app, then roll out everywhere

Phase 1 covers the Airtel app bill only. The grouping and language we define here becomes the standard the other channels adopt next.

Phase 1 · NowAirtel app bill

Grouped charges, "why it's more than your plan" summary, plain-language line items.

Phase 2PDF bill

Same groups and the same words as the app.

Phase 2Web & chatbot

The same explanation, reused.

Phase 3Care Service Portal

Agents see exactly what the customer sees.

Analysing the current experience

Who is calling, and what are they asking?

Before designing anything I spent time with the current bill, the care data and the app data: how big the user base is, how many customers call about their bill, and what they ask most.

4.5 lakhbilling calls to customer care every month
19%of customers who viewed the bill in the app still called care
21%CSAT on the bill detail and explanation flow
1 in 5bills include charges beyond the plan rental
25distinct billing scenarios behind those calls
6kinds of question they fall into

What the current bill shows

How might we help every Postpaid, Broadband and Black customer understand why their bill is what it is, in the same words in the app and the PDF, so they don't need to call care to find out?
Problem statement

What's wrong with the current bill

  1. Charges aren't grouped.Plan, usage, add-ons, one-time charges and taxes sit in one flat list, so customers can't scan their bill.
  2. The gap from the plan price isn't explained.Customers on the ₹599 plan see a higher total with no reason, and call to ask why.
  3. Charges use system language.Labels like "IR usage charges" don't tell people what happened, when, or why it cost what it did.
  4. The app and PDF don't match.The same charge is named and grouped differently, so neither feels trustworthy.
  5. Self-serve doesn't resolve it.19% of customers who view their bill in the app still call care.

Benchmarking

15+ platforms, one question: how do they explain a bill?

I studied how telecom, commerce, mobility and food-delivery apps show a bill: how they group charges, explain changes and highlight what matters. Three patterns stood out.

PatternAirtel todaySeen in best-in-classWhat we took
Charges grouped by typeNoCommonPlan · Usage & add-ons · One-time · Taxes
"What changed" summaryYes/no onlyCommonDifference vs last month, with reasons
Plain-language line itemsSystem namesCommonCause · period · amount
Action on the chargeNoSomeTurn off, dispute, check waiver inline
Same words in app and PDFNoSomeOne naming system for both

Wireframes & explorations

Feedback

What leadership and stakeholders changed

The first review produced constructive pushback that reshaped the approach.

Feedback"A full redesign is costly, and customers already know where things are."
→
ChangeKeep the existing visual language and layout; fix the grouping and the words.
Feedback"The PDF and the app must not tell two different stories."
→
ChangeOne group structure and one naming list, used by the app now and the PDF in phase 2.
Feedback"Don't hide support links to cut calls."
→
ChangeKeep support visible, and put the answer first so fewer people need it.
Feedback"Correct charges shouldn't get goodwill waivers."
→
ChangeExplain correct charges clearly; waive only where the customer is eligible.
Round 1 approach

Redesign the bill screen from scratch

→
Aligned approach

Group and explain charges on the bill customers already know

Final design

A bill that explains the gap

First bill

When a customer's very first bill is being generated, we show an estimate and explain how it's calculated.

Bill due

The bill is generated and payment is due: amount, date and late-fee risk up front, with a clear breakup.

Bill paid

After payment, the bill confirms what was paid and keeps the breakup and dates for reference.

Other cases

Charges that change the bill, and advances adjusted over time, each explained in context.

Learnings

What I'm taking forward

01

Start with the data, not the screen

Call reasons told us which explanation mattered most. The ₹599 gap question shaped the whole design.

02

Fix the words before the pixels

The structure mostly worked. Grouping and plain language did more than a visual redesign would have.

03

AI speeds up exploration, not decisions

Claude, Figma Make and ChatGPT got us to more options faster. Data and stakeholder reviews decided which one shipped.

04

Feedback is a design input

The first review moved us from a costly redesign to a focused fix that could ship sooner.

05

One language across channels

Defining groups once for the app made the PDF, web and agent rollout a reuse, not a redesign.

06

Phase the scope

Starting with the app gave us a measurable first release and a standard for every other channel.
